system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Its system prompt is structured in general-, agent-, and environment-level instructions.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: the agent can still proactively check for new messages by browsing the user's inbox
env_context_strategy.note: Tool descriptions injected via <<tool_descriptions>>; agent explores apps with read tools.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: If context length is exceeded during execution, the agent is terminated and the scenario failed.
context_compaction.note: No compaction: exceeding context terminates the run.

observation_format.evidence_quote: interactions happen through the same interfaces and can be either tool calls, or tool output/notification observations

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: The agent performs one tool call per step, formatted as a JSON.
tool_call_format.note: JSON-in-text is default (avoids model-specific tool calling APIs); a code-execution ReAct prompt also ships (REACT_LOOP_CODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT).

tool_count.evidence_quote: a set of apps, including their content, that are typically found on mobile devices such asMessages,Contacts, orCalendar, providing 101 tools in total
tool_count.note: Count for the Mobile environment used by Gaia2; tool count is environment-dependent.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Apps are collections of tools that interact with a data source.
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing primitive in the default Mobile toolset; a Files app exists but its edit semantics are not described.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: these methods are automatically converted into properly formatted tool descriptions that agents can understand and use

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: ARE supports connection of real apps e.g., through Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Our implementation is a ReAct loop (Yao et al., 2023) with some additions.
loop_primitives.note: Environment is event-driven; pre-step/post-step operations around the LLM call.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Take one action at a time and complete the thought/action/observation cycle before proceeding.

multi_agent_topology.note: Default orchestration is a single main agent; app sub-agents reachable via a2a_app_prop config (scenario_runner.py _apply_a2a_config).

delegation_mechanism.note: Opt-in app-agent delegation via a2a config; default proportion 0.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: All interactions with the user are through theAgentUserInterface, with verification triggered upon task completion.
human_in_loop.note: User messages are part of the simulated scenario, not human approval gates; GUI playground allows interactive chat.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: notifications are injected into the agent's context at the beginning of each agent step

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Apps store their data internally rather than relying on external databases.
long_term_memory.note: No cross-run memory described for the default orchestration.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: the orchestration manages pause/resume functionality where validation occurs semi-onlinei.e.between turns
state_persistence.note: Pause/resume within a run; initial_agent_logs can be passed to run_scenario.

self_verification.evidence_quote: To perform a soft check, an LLM judge is prompted with the user task as context, and the arguments from both the agent action and the oracle action as inputs.
self_verification.note: Verifier is harness-side scoring, not fed back to the agent.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Each model is evaluated three times per scenario to account for variance.
retry_policy.note: Repeats are for variance estimation, not retry-on-failure.

rollback.evidence_quote: Apps maintain their own stateEach app starts in the simulation with an initial state and keeps track of changes as agents use its tools

termination_condition.evidence_quote: The agent loop continues until one of the two termination conditions is met: maximum iteration count (200 steps) or not passing verification at the end of a turn.
termination_condition.note: Also 'Successful completion: Agent signals task completion viasend_message_to_user' and context-length exhaustion terminates the run.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: generation limits of 16,000 tokens per turn
cost_controls.note: Cost is reported per scenario but not enforced as a cap in the default loop.

timeouts.evidence_quote:
# Timeout for polling agent response (seconds)
DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT = 600

execution_isolation.note: Default ARE runs the simulated apps in-process locally; gaia2-cli offers a container-based runner (ContainerLauncher).

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: Apps are stateful API interfaces that typically interact with a data source.
filesystem_access.note: Agent acts on simulated in-memory apps including a simulated filesystem, not the host FS.

network_policy.evidence_quote: While our current implementation stores data in memory, users can easily connect SQL databases or other storage systems without changing the core framework.
network_policy.note: Simulated apps; no agent network egress by default (MCP connection to real apps is opt-in).

permission_model.evidence_quote: Tools are role-scoped—agent, user, orenv. For example, certain user tools may be unavailable to the agent due to sensitivity.

tracing.note: EventLog with detailed metadata; JsonScenarioExporter in scenario_runner.py.

replayability.evidence_quote: complete auditability—all actions can be replayed and analyzed
replayability.note: Paper also claims 'The environment runs deterministically given a fixed starting state and seed', but LLM calls are not deterministic.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Pre-QA guardrailsleverage the graph editor described in Section A.5.4 to prevent any annotated DAG of write from saving if it does not satisfyMobile modeling constraints
guardrails.note: Role-scoping of tools restricts which actions the agent may take; guardrails cited are annotation-side.

target_domain.evidence_quote: a set of apps, including their content, that are typically found on mobile devices such asMessages,Contacts, orCalendar
target_domain.note: Simulated personal-assistant app environments (Mobile); 'other' = simulated assistant environments.

open_source.evidence_quote: This project is licensed under the MIT License. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: ARE supports multiple AI model providers through LiteLLM

first_release_date.note: No tag information in evidence; fallback to paper v1 (arXiv 2509.17158, September 2025) — approximate.
